ANY_PY.description: any .py file at any depth, except inside an ignored directory
ANY_PY.source: nondeterminism-scanner/ndscan.py:625-630 walks os.walk(root), prunes IGNORED_DIR_NAMES (ndscan.py:63-66) and keeps every name ending .py
ANY_PY.ignores_source: nondeterminism-scanner/ndscan.py IGNORED_DIR_NAMES, imported and compared by test_the_ignore_lists_equal_their_consumers

TEST_PY.description: a test module: basename starts with test_ or ends with _test.py, at any depth
TEST_PY.source: weak-assertion-scanner/weakassert.py:87-90 is_test_filename, discovered by weakassert.py:93-105 which also prunes dot-directories
TEST_PY.ignores_source: weak-assertion-scanner/weakassert.py IGNORED_DIR_NAMES, imported and compared by test_the_ignore_lists_equal_their_consumers. NOTE it contains 'env' and NOT '.eggs' -- the reverse of ndscan's. Transcribing instead of importing put '.eggs' here and lost 'env', and a test module under env/ was then reported 'certain' for a report it does not move.

TOOL_CLI_PY.description: a .py file directly inside a top-level tool directory (depth 1). doc-validator narrows further to files that build an ArgumentParser AND call parse_args, but a path alone cannot tell, so this rule is deliberately the wider one
TOOL_CLI_PY.source: doc-validator/optioncheck.py:255-262 lists top-level dirs, docval.py:850-861 lists *.py directly inside each and keeps those with has_argument_parser and has_parse_args
TOOL_CLI_PY.ignores_source: doc-validator/docval.py SKIP_DIR_NAMES plus dot names (optioncheck.py:257), imported and compared

TOOL_TRANSCRIPT.description: a file named exactly captured_output.txt directly inside a top-level tool directory
TOOL_TRANSCRIPT.source: index-generator/pipe_scan.py:55-61 and transcript-schema/validate_transcript.py:347-357 use the identical depth-1 predicate; a captured_output.txt at depth 2 (e.g. commit-claim-auditor/fixture/) is invisible to both
TOOL_TRANSCRIPT.ignores_source: index-generator/pipe_scan.py:57 skips only names starting with a dot; transcript-schema/validate_transcript.py:348 also skips __pycache__, so the intersection is dots alone

TOOL_README.description: a README.md directly inside a top-level tool directory
TOOL_README.source: claim-crosscheck/crosscheck.py:1092-1099 requires <dir>/README.md to treat <dir> as a tool; readme-index/readmeindex.py:276-282 the same
TOOL_README.ignores_source: claim-crosscheck/crosscheck.py:1092-1099 filters nothing: any directory containing a README.md is a tool to it

TOOL_JSON.description: a .json file directly inside a top-level tool directory
TOOL_JSON.source: claim-crosscheck/crosscheck.py:900-903 discovers a tool's report by listing *.json next to its README

NEW_TOOL_DIR.description: a path whose first component is not in known_tool_directories, i.e. the change introduces a top-level directory the map has not seen
NEW_TOOL_DIR.source: derived from known_tool_directories. The consumers that count top-level directories -- regression-checker/coverage_audit.py:239-254 and transcript-schema/validate_transcript.py:346-358 -- skip only dot-prefixed names (and __pycache__), so build/ and dist/ are ordinary directories to them. No filesystem access, so the answer is a function of the map and the paths alone.

BASELINED_TOOL_TREE.description: any path inside a top-level directory that has a baselines.json entry. coverage_audit re-runs each baselined tool and hashes its output, so a change to that tool's source OR its fixtures can move the report
BASELINED_TOOL_TREE.source: regression-checker/coverage_audit.py re-runs every tool named in baselines.json and compares the fresh report hash; baselined_tools in this map is that key list, sorted

DECLARED_INPUT.description: a file that report-freshness/manifest.json names in an entry's `inputs` list. Each report's own trigger names the specific path
DECLARED_INPUT.source: report-freshness/manifest.json `inputs`. The first version of this map read the manifest for argv/cwd/expected_exit_code and ignored `inputs` entirely, which made transcript-schema/schema.json and regression-checker/baselines.json invisible

PRODUCER_SOURCE.description: the script that generates a report. Editing a generator changes what it emits, so it moves its own artifact
PRODUCER_SOURCE.source: each report's own `producer` field. Measured: editing a finding message in weak-assertion-scanner/weakassert.py took self_scan_report.json to 'stale'

GONE_TOOL_DIR.description: a top-level directory the change DELETES, declared with --gone-dir. A path list alone cannot tell 'one file removed' from 'the whole directory removed', so it has to be said
GONE_TOOL_DIR.source: regression-checker/coverage_audit.py:239-254 and transcript-schema/validate_transcript.py:346-358 both count top-level directories, so a deletion moves them exactly as a creation does. Measured: rm -rf sortkey-detector took regression-checker, transcript-schema, claim-crosscheck, nondeterminism-scanner and weak-assertion-scanner to 'stale'

ignored_directory_names_note: Removed on purpose. There is no single repository-wide ignore list: ndscan prunes 11 names and NOT .hg or .svn; weakassert prunes those 11 plus every dot-prefixed name; the depth-1 consumers prune dots plus their own small sets; and coverage_audit/validate_transcript prune only dot names and __pycache__ -- so `build/` and `dist/` DO count as new top-level directories there. A single global list suppressed real impacts: measured, creating build/notes.md moved regression-checker and transcript-schema to 'stale' while a global ignore list made this tool answer exit 0. Each rule now carries its own `ignores`.
